notes: This is a FIXTURE, not the adult pack. It carries targetLevel fade_to_black and fixture prose, and it exists so that the packFile validator block, B10's ContentPackRegistry and E9's build script all have a real pack to run against. The adult pack (targetLevel explicit) is a separate artifact built outside this repository; no explicit content of any kind is authored here, ever.

Asset resolution design: every asset a pack override names must be declared in this file's top-level `assets` array as { id, path }, and `path` is a pack-relative path to a file that actually exists inside the pack directory. `assetIds` on an override then names declared asset IDs and nothing else. That is what "resolves inside the pack" means and what the validator checks -- an override may not reach an asset ID out of the base game's registry, because a pack that could would be a pack that breaks when the base game moves an asset, and B10 merges packs by scene ID without the base tree's ID map in hand.

Pack asset IDs live in their own asset.<pack>.* namespace and are deliberately NOT registered as repository stable IDs: a pack is a separate artifact that may or may not be installed, so a base-game record must never be able to reference one.

Packs are validated but not bundled. tools/src/build-content-bundle.mjs builds content/ for Godot; a pack ships as its own .pck (E9) and is discovered at runtime under user://packs/ or res://packs/ (B10).
The two placeholder asset files under assets/ are DUMMY text markers, not artwork. They exist only so that path resolution is a real check rather than a formality.
